findings.failure_path: extraction_overflow counts any skill in current['requested_skills'] as positive evidence. summarize() adds a Claude Skill tool_use to requested_skills as soon as the request appears, before any result. So a compacted context that holds only a failed (is_error) or pending ccl-skills:skill-extraction-workflow request makes the extraction Stop hook exit quietly. That breaks the acceptance rule that failed and pending evidence stays unknown. The unknown-evidence test only uses product-rd-workflow requests, so it never covers this path.
findings.smallest_fix: Check current['completed_skills'] instead of requested_skills in extraction_overflow. Add pending-extraction and failed-extraction tail cases to test_long_history_without_positive_current_evidence_stays_unknown for skill-extraction-gate-stop.sh.

findings.failure_path: stop_notice runs skill-loading.py's module body but only catches OSError, ValueError, TypeError, AttributeError and ImportError. A packaged or vendored skill-loading.py that raises something else (KeyError, SyntaxError, NameError, RuntimeError) escapes stop_notice, and the __main__ wrapper does not catch it either. On the proposed-next path, the shell then prints 'input normalizer failed' instead of the accurate 'unverified: bounded limit' notice. No test covers a broken optional helper, only a missing state directory.
findings.smallest_fix: Catch Exception around the optional helper import and claim in stop_notice, then fall through to the truthful message. Add a test that runs a runtime copy with a skill-loading.py that raises.

findings.failure_path: This is a release-stage candidate for 0.18.4, but H9 (packaged hooks from built assets) and H10 (tag, provenance and registry readback) are still marked pending, and evidence shows the npm and full make lanes failing or unrun. Nothing in the diff shows that the published package ships hooks/skill-extraction-gate-stop.sh, host-input.py and skill-loading.py side by side. If skill-loading.py were left out, suppression would silently turn off and every notice would repeat, i.e. H1 regresses in the packaged runtime. The source-register row still reads 'updated' as if the prevention were complete.
findings.smallest_fix: Block tagging until make npm-publish-dry and npm-host-smoke pass and repeated-overflow behavior is checked from the installed package. Record the result in the plan, or mark the register row pending until then.

concern_results.conclusion: Actor isolation (session, agent and transcript realpath digest plus dev/inode epoch), the atomic mkdir claim under concurrency, and the fallback when state is unsafe or missing all hold in the diff. Recovering evidence for the delivery hook requires completed skills or a handoff in a complete context. One false-positive gap remains: extraction recovery accepts a failed or pending Skill request. Packaged runtime compatibility (H9) and the release (H10) are unverified.

Notice markers only suppress advisory systemMessage output and never skip the transcript scan or grant permission. The one bypass is on the extraction lane: a failed or never-returned extraction Skill tool_use in the post-compaction context silences the gate. Exceptions from the imported helper that are not in the caught tuple escape stop_notice, and the shell then prints a generic, less accurate fallback notice.
